title: Plenty of Rooms
youtube_title: She moved into a CEO's house — and brought her ex's mother
logline: Nora moves into the concrete Ashford house on the hill and brings Peg. The house is huge and nearly windowless, the house rules are as cold as the contract, and Peg rejects every one of them.
hook: In the car up the hill, Theo reads off his tablet: “Ms. Vale's post.” “Deleted three minutes ago.” Out the window, a grey concrete house juts from the hillside — one whole wall, two windows.
mid_hook: Elias: “Plenty of rooms.” He hands her a key and a card with three lines: “Separate rooms.” “Stay out of the study.” “Don't wait on dinner.” Peg reads it and slaps it down: “Number three? No.”
extra_hooks: Peg opens the double-door fridge: bottled water and coffee beans. “You rich people live on takeout?” Theo opens a new file on his tablet: “Mrs. Ashford Observation Log.” “Day one. No smile.”
conflict: Nora has to live in a stranger's house until the day Grant is sentenced. The house rules are as cold as the contract, and Peg means to cook in a kitchen nobody has ever used.
turn: Nora thought the house only lent her an address. The next night the long table nobody uses holds a full dinner — roast chicken, three sides, a pot of soup. Peg has made it a home.

cliffhanger.text: Next night, nine o'clock. Elias walks in to a full table and three place settings. Peg stands in front of the study door, arms folded: “Sit.” “Eat.”
cliffhanger.question: Will Elias sit down to eat?

spectacle: A grey board-formed concrete house set into the hillside, one wall with only two windows; at night the only light on is the kitchen.
glamour_shot: Elias slips off his coat in the entry — black turtleneck, thin-framed glasses — sees the full table and stops a beat; behind the lenses, for the first time, he looks unsure.
general_payoffs: Nora and Peg each have their own room and key
Peg starts cooking in the Ashford house
locations: The Ashford house on the hill (entry, guest rooms, kitchen, long dining table, study door)

title: Addressed to Mrs. Ashford
youtube_title: Her ex's launch invite came to her new home: “Mrs. Ashford”
logline: Elias sits down at Peg's table. The same night, Whitlock Home's launch invitation arrives at the Ashford house addressed to “Mrs. Ashford,” and Nora knows exactly what her ex wants to see.
hook: Elias looks at Peg for three seconds, takes off his jacket and sits, left hand under the table. He eats every bite. Peg: “Well?” Elias: “…Acceptable.” Peg, to Nora: “That means good.”
mid_hook: Theo sets a gold-foil envelope on the table: the Whitlock Home Forever launch, for “Mrs. Ashford.” Seat card: front row, center. Nora looks a long time: “He wants to see what I wear to cry.”
conflict: Grant has put her front row center so every camera catches the ex-wife “divorced at noon, married to a billionaire by five.” Staying home looks like running. Going looks like walking into it.
turn: Nora reads the invitation as a taunt — until she turns it over. Last item on the program: “Forever No. 1, shown for the first time.” The vase she blew at twenty-five is going on his stage.

cliffhanger.text: Late that night her new phone rings. Sienna: “Mrs. Ashford.” “Dress nice.” “Lots of press.” Someone laughs in the background. Nora knows that laugh. Grant.
cliffhanger.question: How did he get her number?

spectacle: Steam rises off a full dinner on the long concrete table; beside it a gold-foil envelope throws back the ceiling light like a slab of cold metal.
glamour_shot: Nora, shoulder-length hair, plain cream sweater, reads the invitation at the far end of the long table; the overhead light drops a small shadow of lashes on her cheek.
general_payoffs: Elias sits at Peg's table and finishes a full plate
The back of the invitation tells her Forever No. 1 will be on stage
locations: The Ashford house on the hill (long dining table, guest room)

title: Factory-Made, No Name
youtube_title: His store says he designed her vase. She flips every one
logline: Nora pulls the SIM from the phone Grant handed back and goes to see Forever at Whitlock Home's flagship store. Every factory vase is identical, and every one is missing something.
hook: She pops the SIM out of the phone and lays it face down in a drawer: “This one's his.” Next day she opens a line with her own money. Peg writes in the ledger: “Phone line, $30.”
mid_hook: The flagship window: a huge poster, “Forever No. 1 — First Showing.” The clerk smiles: “Mr. Whitlock designed it himself.” Nora: “Did he.”
conflict: Nora needs something to stand on at the launch. Hundreds of Forever vases fill the shelves, all machine-pressed, all identical, not one flaw to find.
turn: She turns the vases over one by one under the light. Every base is clean — not one bubble. Now she's sure: only the one she blew by hand has something inside.

cliffhanger.text: Back at the Ashford house she slides the invitation across to Peg, “No. 1” side up: “There's something inside No. 1.” “He's never seen it.”
cliffhanger.question: What's hidden inside No. 1?

spectacle: On the brightest wall of the flagship store, hundreds of identical Forever vases stand in rows; under the spotlights each one is clean and blank.
glamour_shot: She holds a factory Forever upside down to the case light, hair tucked behind her ear, squinting at the base — for a second she's back at the furnace.
general_payoffs: She pays for her own phone line and cuts Grant's line to her
She confirms the factory vases have no bubbles; only No. 1 does
locations: The Ashford house on the hill (guest room)

title: You're the One on Stage
youtube_title: He left a grey gown at her door: “You're the one on stage.”
logline: Elias gives her the invitation and a misty-grey gown and says he'll be in the audience. The gown fits exactly. So does the color.
hook: At the study door, Elias sets the invitation on a long box and hands it over with his right hand. Inside: a misty-grey gown. “You're the one on stage.” “I'll be in the audience.” He shuts the study door.
mid_hook: She puts it on in front of the mirror. It fits. Misty grey — the color she wore at the furnace at nineteen, and not once in six years of marriage.
extra_hooks: She nudges the box back an inch: “I'll pay for the dress.” Peg has already written it in the ledger: “One gown.” “Owed to Ashford.”
conflict: Nora wants to go up there in her own clothes, on her own two hands. She can't afford a decent dress, and anything he gives her can be called bought.
turn: She assumed he was just opening a door, per clause two. But the gown fits like she was measured, in a color even she had nearly forgotten.

cliffhanger.text: She runs to the study door holding up her hem: “How did you know I love this color?” The door is open, the room empty. Theo leans over the banister: “He says he didn't.”
cliffhanger.question: How did he know about grey?

spectacle: At the end of the concrete hallway stands a floor-length mirror; a misty-grey gown turns slowly against the cold white wall.
glamour_shot: In the misty-grey gown at the mirror — shoulder-length hair, a clean neckline — her own reflection stops her, like someone she hasn't seen in years.
general_payoffs: She has a gown for the stage, logged as a debt in Peg's ledger
She promises herself: on stage, only her own hands
locations: The Ashford house on the hill (study door, hallway, floor-length mirror)

title: Cease and Desist
youtube_title: Her ex's lawyer warned her off. She picked up the gown
logline: The size came from Peg. But three days before the launch, Leonard Fisk sends a cease-and-desist letter warning her off the stage — and Elias can't even tell her “go.”
hook: Peg leans out of the kitchen: “The size was me.” “Six years her mother-in-law.” She points at Theo: “He asked.” Theo pushes up his glasses: “The boss told me to.”
mid_hook: Certified mail: a cease-and-desist letter from Leonard Fisk's office. “Should you disrupt the event or damage any exhibit,” “we will pursue every legal remedy.”
extra_hooks: Dana on the phone: “Going is your call.” “I won't tell you yes.” On the stairs, Elias stands and looks once. He doesn't come down.
conflict: Fisk strikes first: touch anything on that stage and it's disruption and damage. Her lawyer and her husband are both holding to clause two. Nobody will tell her to go or stay.
turn: Nora reads the letter as “stay home.” On the second read she gets it: Fisk isn't afraid she'll show up. He's afraid she'll touch No. 1. They don't know what's in it — but they're scared she does.

cliffhanger.text: Three things side by side on the long table: the letter, the invitation, the grey gown. She looks a long time, folds the letter under the others, and picks up the gown.
cliffhanger.question: Will she still take the stage?

spectacle: A pendant light over the concrete table: the cease-and-desist letter, the gold-foil invitation and a folded grey gown in a row, like three cards she has to pick from.
glamour_shot: Reading the letter, her hair falls along her cheek; at the words “damage any exhibit,” the corner of her mouth moves, barely.
general_payoffs: The gown size came from Peg; nobody answers about the color
She decides to go to the launch

title: Every Woman Who Keeps a Home
youtube_title: Her ex sat her front row, then swung the spotlight onto her
logline: Nora walks into the Forever launch in the grey gown. On stage, Grant calls her vase a tribute to women who keep a home — then turns the spotlight on her.
hook: Under the flagship stage, she has just taken her seat — front row, center — when a wall of camera flashes swings toward her at once. The seat card reads: “Mrs. Ashford.”
mid_hook: Sienna takes the stage to talk inspiration, flipping cue cards with her left hand: “It started with my grandmother's vase.” Center stage, under a glass dome, sits a vase Nora knows by heart — its lip just slightly crooked.
extra_hooks: At the far end of the front row a stocky man flipping a poker chip laughs out loud: “Grant, that vase outsells my condos!” Grant gives him a small bow from the stage.
conflict: Grant wants the whole room to see the remarried ex-wife sitting in the front row. Nora has to find a way to speak on a stage that isn't hers.
turn: She thought she'd just sit there and get photographed. But under that glass dome is the No. 1 she blew at twenty-five — that slight tilt at the lip is her own.

cliffhanger.text: Grant walks downstage with the mic: “Forever.” “For every woman who keeps a home.” “My ex-wife is here tonight.” “I wish her well.” The spotlight swings — white light full on her face, every lens turning with it.
cliffhanger.question: Will she lower her eyes?

spectacle: A glass dome at the center of a black stage, the white vase inside glowing under the top light; in the front row, a spotlight cuts across one face like a blade.
glamour_shot: The spotlight finds her — grey gown, shoulder-length hair. Everyone waits for her to look down. She slowly lifts her chin.
general_payoffs: She reads the seat card for what it is: every camera on the remarried ex-wife
She recognizes No. 1 under the glass dome

title: Bring the Light Down
youtube_title: Her ex put her in the spotlight. She said: “Lower it.”
logline: Grant wants the spotlight to make her look down. Nora walks into it and onto the stage, pulls on gloves, and asks the lighting tech for one angle.
hook: She stands up in the spotlight — and walks toward the stage, not the exit. A guard reaches for her. In the second row, Elias stands up. Just stands. The guard's hand stops midair. Elias sits back down.
mid_hook: At the glass dome she pulls on the white cotton gloves by the plinth and looks up at the lighting booth: “Lights.” “Bring it down a little, please.”
extra_hooks: Grant laughs into the mic: “My ex-wife is a little emotional—” She doesn't turn around: “Two minutes.” “Then talk.”
conflict: She has to show the room what's inside that vase before security walks her off — without damaging a single exhibit, with Fisk's letter still in her clutch.
turn: The crowd expects her to grab the mic and make a scene. She says nothing — she just asks the lighting tech for an angle. She doesn't want the mic. She wants the light.

cliffhanger.text: Ray the lighting tech hesitates one second, then pulls the fader down. The spot drops low and rakes across the stage. She lifts No. 1 out of the dome with both hands and turns it upside down.
cliffhanger.question: What's in the base of No. 1?

spectacle: On a black stage a spotlight slowly lowers into a raking beam; dust motes light up one by one and drift down onto a pair of white-gloved hands.
glamour_shot: In white gloves she holds the vase in the raking light, the grey hem pooled on the black stage; the beam splits her profile half bright, half dark.
general_payoffs: She takes the stage and gets her hands on her own No. 1
Elias stands up once, and security doesn't touch her again

title: There's a Name Inside
youtube_title: She turned the vase over on his stage. It held her name
logline: In front of the whole room, Nora sends light through the base of No. 1. A line of tiny bubbles spells her initials and wedding date — a trick Walter Pell taught her.
hook: The raking light passes through the base. A line of tiny bubbles rises in the beam and forms two letters and a date: her initials, and her wedding day.
mid_hook: She faces the room: “There's a name inside this vase.” Flashback: nineteen, at the furnace, Walter Pell's hands over hers, turning the blowpipe: “Whatever you make,” “leave your name inside.”
extra_hooks: Phones go up, one after another; the livestream camera on the big screen pushes in on the base. Sienna's cue cards scatter across the floor.
conflict: Nora needs everyone to see, at a glance, who made Forever. Grant still holds the mic, and the room is full of press he invited.
turn: The crowd thinks Forever was just stolen credit. But bubbles like these can only be set while the glass is being blown. No factory vase has them — only the one she made by hand. Grant kept it on a shelf for six years and never noticed.

cliffhanger.text: She sets the vase back under the dome and looks at Grant: “Six years,” “and you never once turned it over.” Grant takes the mic from the host, his smile back in place: “My ex-wife—”
cliffhanger.question: How will Grant spin this?

spectacle: On the big screen, the raking light passes through the base and tiny bubbles float up like stars into two letters and a date; below, a hundred phone screens light up at once.
glamour_shot: Light through the base scatters points of brightness across her cheek and lashes; she looks out at the room, calm as freshly annealed glass.
general_payoffs: The whole room sees the bubbles: Forever holds her initials and wedding date
She says it in public: Forever was her wedding gift, blown at twenty-five
locations: Flashback: Furnace No. 3 at Pell Glassworks, twelve years ago

title: I'll Be in the Audience
youtube_title: He called her unstable. Then the press asked about the label
logline: Grant tries to paint her as an unstable ex-wife. The questions turn on him instead — and Elias, in the second row, answers once and says nothing more.
hook: Grant, into the mic: “My ex-wife hasn't quite recovered.” “That's a memory from our marriage.” In the front row, Lyle Becker raises his hand: “Then why isn't her name on the label?”
mid_hook: A mic swings to the second row: “Mr. Ashford, did you set this up?” Elias doesn't stand: “She's the one on stage.” “I'm in the audience.” Then nothing more.
extra_hooks: On the way out, a text from Dana: “You wore gloves.” “You held your own name.” “That letter's got nothing.”
conflict: Grant wants the bubbles to be a marriage keepsake and Nora to be unstable. She needs this to stay about who made the vase, not about the poor ex-wife.
turn: Grant thought the press was his. But once the camera caught that base, the press wanted the story. The more he says “our memory,” the more it sounds like the vase is hers.

cliffhanger.text: She steps off the stage and her phone buzzes. Grant: “Backstage.” “I have something to show you.” The screen lights her face; down the corridor, a light flickers once.
cliffhanger.question: What's he got backstage?

spectacle: After the launch the dome is carried off, but the big screen stays frozen on one frame: a line of glowing bubbles in the base.
glamour_shot: Elias in the second row — charcoal suit, thin-framed glasses — ringed by microphones and still seated, lifts his eyes once to her on stage.
general_payoffs: The press asks about the name on the label, and Grant has no answer
The cease-and-desist can't touch her: she held her own name and damaged nothing

title: Then Prove It
youtube_title: He showed her a signature she never signed: “Prove it.”
logline: Backstage, Grant produces a transfer of the Forever design rights with her signature on it. He tells her to prove it isn't hers — and Elias, at the end of the corridor, can't take one step toward her.
hook: Backstage corridor. Grant blocks her way, smiling warmly: “You signed the rights to the company before the wedding.” He hands her a copy. Her name is on the signature line.
mid_hook: She stares at the signature a long time. It matches the one on the property agreement, every stroke in the same place. “That's not my signature.” Grant: “Then prove it.”
extra_hooks: He leans in, voice low: “You said the property agreement wasn't you, either.” “Who's a judge going to believe?”
conflict: The bubbles prove Nora made Forever; the transfer says she handed the rights to the company before the wedding. She says she never signed it. Grant says prove it.
turn: She thought she'd won tonight, but Grant had the next page ready. Still, staring at the signature, she sees it: the transfer and the property agreement look printed from the same sheet. She couldn't sign exactly alike twice in ten tries.

cliffhanger.text: At the end of the corridor, Elias stands waiting, left hand in his pocket, and doesn't take a single step. Theo, quietly: “Boss, aren't you going over?” Elias: “Clause two.” Nora grips the copy and looks up at him.
cliffhanger.question: How does she prove it's fake?

spectacle: A long backstage corridor with only a few lights on; a photocopy glows white between two people, and at the far end stands a figure who doesn't move.
glamour_shot: The corridor's last light falls on Elias — charcoal suit, straight shoulders, left hand in his pocket. He watches her and doesn't take a step.
general_payoffs: She sees the signatures on the transfer and the property agreement are identical, stroke for stroke
She has a copy of the Forever design-rights transfer
